question: A motor of power $P_0$ is used to deliver water at a certain rate through a given horizontal pipe. To increase the rate of flow of water through the same pipe $n$ times, the power of the motor is increased to $P_1$. The ratio of $P_1$ to $P_0$ is
solution:
Through the same pipe, the rate of flow $Av$ increases $n$ times only if the speed $v$ increases $n$ times.

Power = kinetic energy delivered per second $= \dfrac{1}{2}(\rho Av)v^2 \propto v^3$.

So $P_1 : P_0 = n^3 : 1$.
